figures.title: Chapter map: the transport ledger
figures.why: the topic is one extra ledger on top of the energy accounts — how heat moves and what resists it
figures.data: 8 chapters: vocabulary → expansion → calorimetry → conduction → convection → radiation → Olympiad toolkit → gauntlet
figures.read: chapters 3–4 are the money (budget lines and resistor sums); 5–6 are the two film stories; 7 is the Olympiad floor

figures.title: Three words, one sign rule
figures.why: almost every obvious wrong answer in calorimetry is a slip between T, Q and U; name which quantity a phrase refers to
figures.data: T = pointer (state); Q = joules in transit (process); U = balance (state); ΔU = Q − W_by (Q > 0 in, W_by > 0 out)
figures.read: a body does not 'contain heat' — it stores U; heat is a verb disguised as a noun
figures.source: §1.1 Three words that must never be mixed up

figures.title: The final-state algorithm: budget before you solve
figures.why: mixing answers are decided by which side exhausts first; solving mcΔT before checking the plateau is the biggest mark-loss
figures.data: budget both sides to the nearest plateau → if supply < demand, T_final = plateau T and the answer is a mass fraction → else solve mcΔT legs
figures.read: whichever plateau is still occupied sets the temperature; steam cannot lift ice past 0 °C

figures.title: Conduction is a resistor network
figures.why: every wall, pipe and junction is Ohm's law for heat; the R-chain turns interface-temperature and condensation questions into resistor arithmetic
figures.data: R = L/(kA); series adds R, parallel adds conductance; ΔT_i = Q̇ R_i; pipe R = ln(r₂/r₁)/(2πkL)
figures.read: 50 mm of insulation resists four times more than 220 mm of brick — the log of a pipe is only a different R

figures.title: Newton's law is an RC discharge
figures.why: Newton's cooling is Fourier through a film — one time constant answers every 'time to reach T' and 'read h from the curve' question
figures.data: T(t) − T∞ = (T₀ − T∞)e^(−t/τ), τ = mc/(hA) = R_th C_th, t_1/2 = 0.69 τ
figures.read: two data points on a cooling curve give both the ambient and the conductance

figures.title: The trap shelf: ten ways to lose the mark
figures.why: the topic's losses are a short list, each with a one-line fix, so the shelf doubles as a pre-exam checklist
figures.data: U vs Q; sign rule; holes grow; stress two-step; −3γ_glass; budget first; steady ≠ no-flow; plane vs log R; Biot licence; subtract the room's radiation
figures.read: every warning is a sentence you already know — re-read them the night before, not the week after
